    AI Overview
    The Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) is an annual, multi-day gathering of conservative activists, politicians, and media personalities, typically hosted by the
    American Conservative Union. Known as a major "America First" event, it acts as a premier networking venue for the Republican movement and a indicator of party direction. 
    Key details about CPAC include: 
    • Purpose: It brings together grassroots activists, elected officials, and thought leaders for networking, speeches, and training sessions.
    • Atmosphere: Known as a mix of political rallies, "conservative boot camp," and trade shows, it frequently highlights leading figures in the modern conservative movement.
    • Influence: It is considered one of the largest and most influential gatherings of its kind, often showcasing potential political candidates or the current direction of the party.
    • 2026 Event: As of late March 2026, the event was held in Grapevine, Texas, featuring discussions on issues like the "America First" agenda and the economy. 
    Note: There are other entities with similar acronyms, such as Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) financing, but this refers to the Conservative Political Action Conference.
